parsed_response.reasoning: Verified against the diff: parseRefreshTokenResponse is imported/used only in googlecalendar/CalendarService.ts, office365calendar/CalendarService.ts, zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts, and salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts. The other rewired refresh sites (hubspot, larkcalendar, office365video, webex, zoho-bigin, zohocrm) wrap their refresh calls in refreshOAuthTokens but apply no sharing-mode schema validation before persisting. This is a real, specific inconsistency created by this diff: in sharing-enabled deployments, a malformed CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT response is rejected for some apps and persisted unvalidated for others. It is not a defect in default (non-sharing) deployments since the sharing path is opt-in, so it fits the substantive-scope/incomplete-coverage advisory category rather than a confirmed bug.

judged_text: The sharing-mode response validation (parseRefreshTokenResponse) is applied at only four of the ten refresh sites this PR rewires (google, office365-calendar, zoom, salesforce); msteams, hubspot, lark, webex, zoho-bigin and zohocrm receive sharing-mode responses with no validation at all. In sharing deployments a malformed endpoint response fails loudly for the validated apps but is persisted unvalidated for the other six, so the same parent-app bug produces inconsistent corruption across apps and is far harder to diagnose.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `parseRefreshTokenResponse` for “sharing mode” validation but only wires it into some refresh paths: GoogleCalendar (`googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`), Office365Calendar (`office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`), Zoom (`zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts`), and Salesforce (`salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`). Other refresh sites modified to use `refreshOAuthTokens` (e.g., Hubspot, Lark, Webex, Zoho Bigin, Zoho CRM, Office365 video) do not use `parseRefreshTokenResponse` in the shown diff. That creates an inconsistency in how refreshed-token payloads are shape-checked under sharing mode. However, the finding’s stronger claim that the other apps “receive sharing-mode responses with no validation at all” and that malformed responses are “persisted” isn’t fully verifiable from this diff alone (some flows may validate inside other helpers like `handleWebexResponse`, and persistence isn’t always shown).
